name: ArtifactUrl
title: Artifact URL
description: An absolute URI that is used to identify this artifact when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this artifact is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the artifact is stored on different servers.
purpose: This extension is defined to support representing artifact metadata on resources that are not already canonical resources that have the corresponding element, and that behave in a definitional way. For example, it would not be appropriate to use this extension on a patient-specific resource such as MedicationRequest or CarePlan. For resources where this element was added in R5, the cross-version extension should be used rather than this extension (ConditionDefinition,NamingSystem,ObservationDefinition,SpecimenDefinition,SubscriptionTopic).

element.short: Canonical identifier for this artifact, represented as a URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this artifact when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this artifact is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the artifact is stored on different servers.
element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred.  Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author.  Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions). 

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.

element.short: identifies the meaning of the extension
element.definition: Source of the definition for the extension code - a logical name or a URL.
element.comment: The definition may point directly to a computable or human-readable definition of the extensibility codes, or it may be a logical URI as declared in some other specification. The definition SHALL be a URI for the Structure Definition defining the extension.

element.definition: Value of extension - must be one of a constrained set of the data types (see [Extensibility](http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/extensibility.html) for a list).
